<content>
1: # opencode-container
2: 
3: Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.
4: 
5: ## Quickstart
6: 
7: **Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).
8: 
9: ```bash
10: make build
11: make serve
12: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
13: ```
14: 
15: That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.
16: 
17: ## Containers
18: 
19: | Container | Dockerfile | Mode | Port | Profiles | Volumes | Purpose |
20: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
21: | `opencode-serve` | `serve.dockerfile` | `serve` | 4096 | — | data, config | Headless HTTP server: web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc. Starts with an initialized git project. |
22: | `opencode-web` | `web.dockerfile` | `web` | 4098 | — | data, config | Same as `serve` but uses `opencode web` (auto-instantiates a project on first load). |
23: | `opencode-acp` | `acp.dockerfile` | `acp` | 4097 | — | — | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via `socat`. For ACP-compatible clients (Cline, continue.dev). |
24: | `opencode-issue-processor` | `issue-processor.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | Batch: iterates all open issues from configured repos, pipes each into `opencode run`. Exits when done. |
25: | `opencode-plan-issue` | `plan-issue.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | One-shot: clones a repo, analyzes a specific issue, posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment. Exits when done. |
26: | `opencode-generic-worker` | `generic-worker.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config from a mounted volume, execute a mounted script or inline command. |
27: 
28: ### Which container do I pick?
29: 
30: | You want to... | Use |
31: |---|---|
32: | Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` (`make serve`) |
33: | Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` (`make web`) |
34: | Connect an ACP client (e.g. Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` (`make acp`) |
35: | Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` (`make process`) |
36: | Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` (`make plan`) |
37: | Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` (`make generic`) |
38: | Run a continuous issue-resolution workflow | `workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` |
39: | Pass `--help` flags to opencode | `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` |
40: 
41: ### Managing repos for the issue processor
42: 
43: The issue processor (`process-issues.sh`) hardcodes target repositories:
44: 
45: ```bash
46: REPOS=(
47:   "tbrandenburg/made"
48:   "tbrandenburg/pyrag"
49: )
50: ```
51: 
52: Edit this array in `process-issues.sh` to change which repos it scans for open issues. Each entry is an `owner/repo` pair understood by `gh issue list`.
53: 
54: ## Architecture
55: 
56: ### Why this design?
57: 
58: OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements. Rather than crafting a single monolithic image, each mode gets its own Dockerfile. This gives us:
59: 
60: - **Isolation by purpose**: A `socat` dependency for ACP doesn't bloat the serve image. Git and `gh` CLI for runners don't affect the server image.
61: - **Independent lifecycle**: Serve/web containers run long-term. Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker) are ephemeral — they clone, execute, and exit.
62: - **Clean `--help` passthrough**: Serve/web use `ENTRYPOINT` so `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` works naturally. Runner containers use `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` pointing to their shell scripts.
63: 
64: #### serve vs web — what's the difference?
65: 
66: Both `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web` run HTTP servers. The difference:
67: 
68: - **`serve`** (`opencode serve`): Requires an existing git-initialized project. The Dockerfile creates one at build time (`git init` + commit). Good for teams that want to control the project lifecycle.
69: - **`web`** (`opencode web`): Auto-instantiates a project on first load. Slightly more self-service for new users.
70: 
71: Pick `serve` for production/team setups where you mount your own project. Pick `web` for quick experiments.
72: 
73: #### Why socat for ACP?
74: 
75: OpenCode's ACP mode speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over **stdin/stdout** — it's designed for local processes, not network sockets. To make it accessible inside Docker without modifying OpenCode itself, `socat` bridges a TCP listener to the process's stdio:
76: 
77: ```
78: TCP client → socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 → EXEC:"opencode acp" (stdin/stdout)
79: ```
80: 
81: This is a classic Unix pattern: a small, trusted tool adapts a stdio protocol to the network. It works on any port, requires zero OpenCode changes, and the container is completely transparent about it.
82: 
83: #### Why the profile/manual pattern?
84: 
85: ```yaml
86: profiles:
87:   - manual
88: ```
89: 
90: Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:
91: 
92: ```bash
93: docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
94: ```
95: 
96: This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.
97: 
98: #### Why volume sharing?
99: 
100: All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:
101: 
102: | Volume | Mount point | Contents |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
105: | `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |
106: 
107: This means:
108: - Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
109: - Server and runner containers share the same config and history
110: - Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`
111: 
112: ### The workflows pattern
113: 
114: The `workflows/` directory contains reusable OpenCode workflow harnesses — shell scripts that orchestrate multi-step agent tasks in a structured, logged fashion. Each workflow:
115: 
116: 1. Clones or assumes a repository working copy
117: 2. Runs a sequence of steps (bash commands and/or `opencode` agent invocations)
118: 3. Logs everything to a dedicated log file with ISO-8601 timestamps
119: 4. Supports `--dry-run` for previewing without side effects
120: 
121: The main workflow:
122: - **`workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh`**: A full issue lifecycle workflow — checks for open issues, syncs main, fixes via agent, commits/pushes, resolves CI errors, reviews the PR, raises follow-up issues, and merges. Intended to run inside the `generic-worker` container.
123: 
124: Workflow harness scripts implement these functions:
125: - `log()` — ISO-8601 UTC timestamped logging to stderr + log file
126: - `run_step()` — execute a bash function step with failure handling, output streaming via `tee`
127: - `run_agent()` — pipe a prompt to `opencode run --format json` with optional `--agent` selector
128: - `catch()` — centralized failure hook that logs the step name and exit code
129: 
130: ### Shell script robustness
131: 
132: Every `.sh` file in the repo root uses `set -euo pipefail` and validates required environment variables with descriptive error messages before proceeding. Shell scripts pass `shellcheck` at warning level with zero errors.
133: 
134: ### Base image
135: 
136: All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
137: - `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
138: - `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
139: - `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
140: - `socat` for the ACP bridge container
141: 
142: ### Network ports
143: 
144: ### Network isolation
145: 
146: Docker Compose creates a default bridge network (`opencode-container_default`). All containers within `docker-compose.yml` are on this network and can reach each other by service name (e.g., `http://opencode-serve:4096` from another container).
147: 
148: | Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Network | Auth |
149: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
150: | `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | bridge (default) | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
151: | `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | bridge (default) | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
152: | `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | bridge (default) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |
153: 
154: Runner containers (`manual` profile) have no published ports but are reachable by service name on the same network for outbound connections.
155: 
156: ## Environment Variables
157: 
158: | Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
159: |---|---|---|---|---|
160: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | HTTP Basic auth password. Override in docker-compose.yml or via `-e`. |
161: | `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`, workflow harnesses | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | GitHub personal access token. Pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` at runtime. Never hardcoded in any Dockerfile or script — only interpolated by the calling shell. Never enters agent context. |
162: | `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`. The script parses owner/repo/number from this URL. |
163: | `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL. The generic worker validates this is non-empty before proceeding. |
164: | `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number passed as an environment variable to the child command or script. |
165: | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/opencode-config` | Source directory (inside container) to copy config from when bootstrapping. Mount a host config directory here to inject custom agents. |
166: | `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/repo` | Destination directory for `git clone`. |
167: | `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped opencode global config. |
168: | `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | no (build ARG) | `amd64` | Docker build `--build-arg` for architecture-specific `gh` CLI download. Set `--build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` on ARM hosts. |
169: | `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` in Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |
170: | `FLOWSH_LOG_DIR` | Test harness scripts (`tests/generic-worker/.harness/*.sh`) | no | `.flowsh/logs` | Override the log directory for generated flowsh harness scripts. Only relevant when developing or debugging test harnesses. |
171: 
172: ### Env var security rules
173: 
174: - `GH_TOKEN` is **never hardcoded** in any Dockerfile or `.sh` file. It is passed at container runtime from the calling shell's `gh auth token` output.
175: - `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` has a default value of `changeme` in both Dockerfiles and `docker-compose.yml`. Change it in production.
176: 
177: ## Commands
178: 
179: | Command | Description |
180: |---|---|
181: | `make install` | No-op (containers are self-contained). Prints informational message. |
182: | `make build` | `docker compose build` — builds all container images. |
183: | `make run` | `docker compose up -d` — starts all server containers in background. |
184: | `make stop` | `docker compose down` — stops all containers. |
185: | `make serve` | `docker compose up -d opencode-serve` — start only the headless server. |
186: | `make web` | `docker compose up -d opencode-web` — start only the web UI server. |
187: | `make acp` | `docker compose up -d opencode-acp` — start only the ACP bridge. |
188: | `make logs` | `docker compose logs -f` — follow logs from all running containers. |
189: | `make clean` | `docker compose down --remove-orphans -v` — stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes. |
190: | `make process` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor` — run the issue processor (exit when done). |
191: | `make plan` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue` — run the issue planner (exit when done). |
192: | `make generic` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker` — run the generic worker (exit when done). |
193: | `make lint` | `shellcheck` on all shell scripts (root + tests). |
194: | `make test` | Build + shellcheck + integration tests for all containers. |
195: | `make verify-quickstart` | Automated quickstart verification: build, serve, health-check, cleanup. |
196: | `make test-generic-worker` | Extended generic-worker integration tests (agent harness + repo inspection). |
197: 
198: ### --help passthrough
199: 
200: Because the serve/web containers use the pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for flags, you can pass `--help` directly:
201: 
202: ```bash
203: docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
204: docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
205: ```
206: 
207: ## Usage
208: 
209: ### Server containers (long-running)
210: 
211: ```bash
212: # Build everything
213: make build
214: 
215: # Start all servers
216: make run
217: 
218: # Start individual server
219: docker compose up -d opencode-serve
220: 
221: # Health check
222: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
223: 
224: # View logs
225: make logs
226: 
227: # Stop everything
228: make stop
229: ```
230: 
231: ### Issue processor (batch, then exit)
232: 
233: ```bash
234: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
235: ```
236: 
237: The processor (`process-issues.sh`) iterates all open issues from hardcoded repos, piping each issue number into `opencode run`. Configure which repos to scan by editing `process-issues.sh`.
238: 
239: ### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)
240: 
241: ```bash
242: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/30 \
243:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
244:   make plan
245: ```
246: 
247: The planner (`plan-issue.sh`) parses the issue URL to extract owner/repo/number, clones the repo, then pipes a prompt into `opencode run` instructing it to read the issue, understand the codebase, and post a plan as a GitHub comment.
248: 
249: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
250: 
251: ```bash
252: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
253: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
254:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
255:   -e ISSUE=42 \
256:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
257:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
258:   /script.sh
259: 
260: # Pass an inline command instead:
261: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
262:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
263:   -e ISSUE=42 \
264:   sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
265: ```
266: 
267: The worker (`generic-worker.sh`):
268: 1. Validates `REPO_URL` is set
269: 2. Clones the repo to `WORK_DIR` (default `/repo`)
270: 3. If `/opencode-config` exists (from a mounted volume), copies it to `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` to bootstrap custom agent definitions
271: 4. Exports `ISSUE` as an environment variable
272: 5. Executes the provided command (or exits with clone info if no command given)
273: 
274: **Security**: `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` are passed from the host environment and never read into agent context.
275: 
276: ## Testing
277: 
278: ```bash
279: make build    # Build all images first (required)
280: make test     # Run shellcheck + all integration tests
281: make verify-quickstart  # Full quickstart verification (build → serve → curl → cleanup)
282: ```
283: 
284: The test suite (`tests/`) exercises:
285: 
286: | Test file | What it validates |
287: |---|---|
288: | `test-serve.sh` | `opencode-serve --help` returns help text |
289: | `test-web.sh` | `opencode-web --help` returns help text |
290: | `test-acp.sh` | socat binary is present, opencode binary is present |
291: | `test-generic-worker.sh` | Missing `REPO_URL` triggers error; clone-and-inspect on a real public repo |
292: | `test-issue-processor.sh` | Missing `GH_TOKEN` triggers error |
293: | `test-plan-issue.sh` | Missing `ISSUE_URL` triggers error |
294: | `verify-quickstart.sh` | End-to-end: `make build`, `make serve`, curl health-check, `make stop` |
295: | `generic-worker/run-tests.sh` | Extended agent harness + repo inspection (requires `GH_TOKEN`). Runs as part of `make test` when `GH_TOKEN` is set. |
296: 
297: ### Extended generic-worker test suite
298: 
299: The `tests/generic-worker/` directory contains an extended integration test suite for the generic worker container:
300: 
301: | File | Purpose |
302: |---|---|
303: | `run-tests.sh` | Test runner: invokes both harnesses inside the container |
304: | `.harness/agent_test.sh` | Bootstraps a custom agent and runs `opencode run --agent test` |
305: | `.harness/repo_inspect.sh` | Non-destructive: git log, file count, README check on a cloned repo |
306: | `agent/test.md` | Custom test agent definition ("test" agent) |
307: | `.made/workflows.yml` | Workflow definition metadata |
308: 
309: These tests require `GH_TOKEN` for GitHub operations and are skipped by `make test` if the token is unavailable. Run them explicitly:
310: 
311: ```bash
312: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make test-generic-worker
313: ```
314: 
315: ### Workflow harness tests
316: 
317: The `workflows/issue-resolution/` directory contains a continuous issue-resolution workflow:
318: 
319: | Path | Purpose |
320: |---|---|
321: | `.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` | Full issue lifecycle: check issues, sync, fix, commit, review, merge |
322: | `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` | OpenCode config for the workflow (Context7 + sequential thinking MCP) |
323: | `.opencode/agent/review.md` | Custom review agent definition |
324: | `.opencode/commands/` | Command files: `prp-issue-fix.md`, `prp-review.md`, `commit-push.md`, `resolve-ci-errors.md`, and `ghar-*` variants |
325: | `.made/workflows.yml` | Workflow metadata |
326: 
327: Run the continuous resolution workflow inside the generic-worker:
328: 
329: ```bash
330: docker compose run --rm \
331:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
332:   -e GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
333:   -v "$(pwd)/workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro" \
334:   opencode-generic-worker \
335:   /path/to/continuous-issue-resolution.sh
336: ```
337: 
338: ## Security Rules
339: 
340: 1. **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Always pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
341: 2. **Change the default password** in production: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` to a strong value.
342: 3. **`profiles: [manual]`** containers must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — never started by `docker compose up`.
343: 4. **Container entrypoints use `set -euo pipefail`** and validate required environment variables before proceeding.
344: 5. **Secrets never enter agent context** — runner containers pass tokens as env vars only, not as part of agent prompts.
345: 
346: ## Prerequisites
347: 
348: | Tool | Minimum version | Purpose |
349: |---|---|---|
350: | [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) | 24+ (Compose v2) | Container runtime |
351: | [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) | 2.x | GitHub authentication for runner containers |
352: 
353: Docker must be installed and the Docker socket accessible. The `gh` CLI is only required if you use the runner containers (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`).
354: 
355: ## Project Structure
356: 
357: ```
358: .
359: ├── serve.dockerfile          # HTTP server image
360: ├── web.dockerfile            # Web UI server image
361: ├── acp.dockerfile            # ACP protocol bridge image
362: ├── issue-processor.dockerfile # Batch issue processor image
363: ├── plan-issue.dockerfile      # Single-issue planner image
364: ├── generic-worker.dockerfile  # Generic clone-and-exec worker image
365: ├── generic-worker.sh          # Entrypoint script for generic-worker
366: ├── plan-issue.sh              # Entrypoint script for plan-issue
367: ├── process-issues.sh          # Entrypoint script for issue-processor
368: ├── docker-compose.yml         # All service definitions, volumes, profiles
369: ├── Makefile                   # All make targets (build/run/test/lint/clean/verify-quickstart)
370: ├── tests/                     # Integration test suite
371: │   ├── test-serve.sh
372: │   ├── test-web.sh
373: │   ├── test-acp.sh
374: │   ├── test-generic-worker.sh
375: │   ├── test-issue-processor.sh
376: │   ├── test-plan-issue.sh
377: │   ├── verify-quickstart.sh
378: │   └── generic-worker/        # Extended generic-worker tests
379: │       ├── run-tests.sh
380: │       ├── .harness/          # Test harness scripts
381: │       └── agent/             # Custom test agent definitions
382: ├── workflows/                 # Workflow harness definitions
383: │   └── issue-resolution/      # Continuous issue resolution workflow
384: │       ├── .harness/
385: │       ├── .opencode/         # OpenCode config, agents, commands
386: │       └── .made/
387: └── AGENTS.md                  # Project-level agent instructions
388: ```
389: 
390: ## Dockerfiles detail
391: 
392: ### Base pattern (all containers)
393: 
394: ```dockerfile
395: FROM node:22-slim
396: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
397:     git ca-certificates [socat] [curl] && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
398: RUN npm install -g opencode-ai@latest
399: ```
400: 
401: ### Serve & Web
402: 
403: ```dockerfile
404: ENV OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=changeme
405: EXPOSE 4096
406: ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve"]
407: CMD ["--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"]
408: ```
409: 
410: ### ACP
411: 
412: ```dockerfile
413: EXPOSE 4097
414: CMD socat TCP-LISTEN:4097,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"opencode acp",pty,stderr
415: ```
416: 
417: No `ENTRYPOINT` — uses `CMD` directly so socat is the main process.
418: 
419: ### Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker)
420: 
421: ```dockerfile
422: ARG TARGETARCH
423: RUN case "$TARGETARCH" in ... download gh CLI ... esac
424: COPY *.sh /usr/local/bin/
425: CMD ["/usr/local/bin/script.sh"]  # or ENTRYPOINT for generic-worker
426: ```
427: 
428: ## License
429: 
430: MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

</content>

### Managing repos for the issue processor

The issue processor (`process-issues.sh`) defaults to a hardcoded list:

```bash
REPOS=(
  "tbrandenburg/made"
  "tbrandenburg/pyrag"
)

Override at runtime with the `REPOS` environment variable (comma-separated):

```bash
REPOS=tbrandenburg/pyrag,owner/other-repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process

Edit the array in `process-issues.sh` to change the default list. Each entry is an `owner/repo` pair understood by `gh issue list`.

<path>/home/tom/workspace/ai/made/workspace/opencode-container/README.md</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: # opencode-container
2: 
3: Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.
4: 
5: ## Quickstart
6: 
7: **Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).
8: 
9: ```bash
10: make build
11: make serve
12: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
13: ```
14: 
15: That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.
16: 
17: ## Containers
18: 
19: | Container | Dockerfile | Mode | Port | Profiles | Volumes | Purpose |
20: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
21: | `opencode-serve` | `serve.dockerfile` | `serve` | 4096 | — | data, config | Headless HTTP server: web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc. Starts with an initialized git project. |
22: | `opencode-web` | `web.dockerfile` | `web` | 4098 | — | data, config | Same as `serve` but uses `opencode web` (auto-instantiates a project on first load). |
23: | `opencode-acp` | `acp.dockerfile` | `acp` | 4097 | — | — | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via `socat`. For ACP-compatible clients (Cline, continue.dev). |
24: | `opencode-issue-processor` | `issue-processor.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | Batch: iterates all open issues from configured repos, pipes each into `opencode run`. Exits when done. |
25: | `opencode-plan-issue` | `plan-issue.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | One-shot: clones a repo, analyzes a specific issue, posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment. Exits when done. |
26: | `opencode-generic-worker` | `generic-worker.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config from a mounted volume, execute a mounted script or inline command. |
27: 
28: ### Which container do I pick?
29: 
30: | You want to... | Use |
31: |---|---|
32: | Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` (`make serve`) |
33: | Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` (`make web`) |
34: | Connect an ACP client (e.g. Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` (`make acp`) |
35: | Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` (`make process`) |
36: | Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` (`make plan`) |
37: | Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` (`make generic`) |
38: | Run a continuous issue-resolution workflow | `workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` |
39: | Pass `--help` flags to opencode | `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` |
40: 
41: ### Managing repos for the issue processor
42: 
43: The issue processor (`process-issues.sh`) defaults to a hardcoded list:
44: 
45: ```bash
46: REPOS=(
47:   "tbrandenburg/made"
48:   "tbrandenburg/pyrag"
49: )
50: ```
51: 
52: Override at runtime with the `REPOS` environment variable (comma-separated):
53: 
54: ```bash
55: REPOS=tbrandenburg/pyrag,owner/other-repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
56: ```
57: 
58: Edit the array in `process-issues.sh` to change the default list. Each entry is an `owner/repo` pair understood by `gh issue list`.
59: 
60: ## Architecture
61: 
62: ### Why this design?
63: 
64: OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements. Rather than crafting a single monolithic image, each mode gets its own Dockerfile. This gives us:
65: 
66: - **Isolation by purpose**: A `socat` dependency for ACP doesn't bloat the serve image. Git and `gh` CLI for runners don't affect the server image.
67: - **Independent lifecycle**: Serve/web containers run long-term. Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker) are ephemeral — they clone, execute, and exit.
68: - **Clean `--help` passthrough**: Serve/web use `ENTRYPOINT` so `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` works naturally. Runner containers use `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` pointing to their shell scripts.
69: 
70: #### serve vs web — what's the difference?
71: 
72: Both `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web` run HTTP servers. The difference:
73: 
74: - **`serve`** (`opencode serve`): Requires an existing git-initialized project. The Dockerfile creates one at build time (`git init` + commit). Good for teams that want to control the project lifecycle.
75: - **`web`** (`opencode web`): Auto-instantiates a project on first load. Slightly more self-service for new users.
76: 
77: Pick `serve` for production/team setups where you mount your own project. Pick `web` for quick experiments.
78: 
79: #### Why socat for ACP?
80: 
81: OpenCode's ACP mode speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over **stdin/stdout** — it's designed for local processes, not network sockets. To make it accessible inside Docker without modifying OpenCode itself, `socat` bridges a TCP listener to the process's stdio:
82: 
83: ```
84: TCP client → socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 → EXEC:"opencode acp" (stdin/stdout)
85: ```
86: 
87: This is a classic Unix pattern: a small, trusted tool adapts a stdio protocol to the network. It works on any port, requires zero OpenCode changes, and the container is completely transparent about it.
88: 
89: #### Why the profile/manual pattern?
90: 
91: ```yaml
92: profiles:
93:   - manual
94: ```
95: 
96: Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:
97: 
98: ```bash
99: docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
100: ```
101: 
102: This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.
103: 
104: #### Why volume sharing?
105: 
106: All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:
107: 
108: | Volume | Mount point | Contents |
109: |---|---|---|
110: | `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
111: | `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |
112: 
113: This means:
114: - Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
115: - Server and runner containers share the same config and history
116: - Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`
117: 
118: ### The workflows pattern
119: 
120: The `workflows/` directory contains reusable OpenCode workflow harnesses — shell scripts that orchestrate multi-step agent tasks in a structured, logged fashion. Each workflow:
121: 
122: 1. Clones or assumes a repository working copy
123: 2. Runs a sequence of steps (bash commands and/or `opencode` agent invocations)
124: 3. Logs everything to a dedicated log file with ISO-8601 timestamps
125: 4. Supports `--dry-run` for previewing without side effects
126: 
127: The main workflow:
128: - **`workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh`**: A full issue lifecycle workflow — checks for open issues, syncs main, fixes via agent, commits/pushes, resolves CI errors, reviews the PR, raises follow-up issues, and merges. Intended to run inside the `generic-worker` container.
129: 
130: Workflow harness scripts implement these functions:
131: - `log()` — ISO-8601 UTC timestamped logging to stderr + log file
132: - `run_step()` — execute a bash function step with failure handling, output streaming via `tee`
133: - `run_agent()` — pipe a prompt to `opencode run --format json` with optional `--agent` selector
134: - `catch()` — centralized failure hook that logs the step name and exit code
135: 
136: ### Shell script robustness
137: 
138: Every `.sh` file in the repo root uses `set -euo pipefail` and validates required environment variables with descriptive error messages before proceeding. Shell scripts pass `shellcheck` at warning level with zero errors.
139: 
140: ### Base image
141: 
142: All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
143: - `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
144: - `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
145: - `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
146: - `socat` for the ACP bridge container
147: 
148: ### Network ports
149: 
150: ### Network isolation
151: 
152: Docker Compose creates a default bridge network (`opencode-container_default`). All containers within `docker-compose.yml` are on this network and can reach each other by service name (e.g., `http://opencode-serve:4096` from another container).
153: 
154: | Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Network | Auth |
155: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
156: | `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | bridge (default) | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
157: | `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | bridge (default) | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
158: | `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | bridge (default) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |
159: 
160: Runner containers (`manual` profile) have no published ports but are reachable by service name on the same network for outbound connections.
161: 
162: ## Environment Variables
163: 
164: | Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
165: |---|---|---|---|---|
166: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | HTTP Basic auth password. Override in docker-compose.yml or via `-e`. |
167: | `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`, workflow harnesses | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | GitHub personal access token. Pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` at runtime. Never hardcoded in any Dockerfile or script — only interpolated by the calling shell. Never enters agent context. |
168: | `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`. The script parses owner/repo/number from this URL. |
169: | `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL. The generic worker validates this is non-empty before proceeding. |
170: | `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number passed as an environment variable to the child command or script. |
171: | `REPOS` | `issue-processor` | no | hardcoded array in `process-issues.sh` | Comma-separated list of `owner/repo` pairs. Overrides the hardcoded default. Example: `REPOS=owner/repo1,owner/repo2`. |
172: | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/opencode-config` | Source directory (inside container) to copy config from when bootstrapping. Mount a host config directory here to inject custom agents. |
173: | `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/repo` | Destination directory for `git clone`. |
174: | `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped opencode global config. |
175: | `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | no (build ARG) | `amd64` | Docker build `--build-arg` for architecture-specific `gh` CLI download. Set `--build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` on ARM hosts. |
176: | `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` in Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |
177: | `FLOWSH_LOG_DIR` | Test harness scripts (`tests/generic-worker/.harness/*.sh`) | no | `.flowsh/logs` | Override the log directory for generated flowsh harness scripts. Only relevant when developing or debugging test harnesses. |
178: 
179: ### Env var security rules
180: 
181: - `GH_TOKEN` is **never hardcoded** in any Dockerfile or `.sh` file. It is passed at container runtime from the calling shell's `gh auth token` output.
182: - `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` has a default value of `changeme` in both Dockerfiles and `docker-compose.yml`. Change it in production.
183: 
184: ## Commands
185: 
186: | Command | Description |
187: |---|---|
188: | `make install` | No-op (containers are self-contained). Prints informational message. |
189: | `make build` | `docker compose build` — builds all container images. |
190: | `make run` | `docker compose up -d` — starts all server containers in background. |
191: | `make stop` | `docker compose down` — stops all containers. |
192: | `make serve` | `docker compose up -d opencode-serve` — start only the headless server. |
193: | `make web` | `docker compose up -d opencode-web` — start only the web UI server. |
194: | `make acp` | `docker compose up -d opencode-acp` — start only the ACP bridge. |
195: | `make logs` | `docker compose logs -f` — follow logs from all running containers. |
196: | `make clean` | `docker compose down --remove-orphans -v` — stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes. |
197: | `make process` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor` — run the issue processor (exit when done). |
198: | `make plan` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue` — run the issue planner (exit when done). |
199: | `make generic` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker` — run the generic worker (exit when done). |
200: | `make lint` | `shellcheck` on all shell scripts (root + tests). |
201: | `make test` | Build + shellcheck + integration tests for all containers. |
202: | `make verify-quickstart` | Automated quickstart verification: build, serve, health-check, cleanup. |
203: | `make test-generic-worker` | Extended generic-worker integration tests (agent harness + repo inspection). |
204: 
205: ### --help passthrough
206: 
207: Because the serve/web containers use the pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for flags, you can pass `--help` directly:
208: 
209: ```bash
210: docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
211: docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
212: ```
213: 
214: ## Usage
215: 
216: ### Server containers (long-running)
217: 
218: ```bash
219: # Build everything
220: make build
221: 
222: # Start all servers
223: make run
224: 
225: # Start individual server
226: docker compose up -d opencode-serve
227: 
228: # Health check
229: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
230: 
231: # View logs
232: make logs
233: 
234: # Stop everything
235: make stop
236: ```
237: 
238: ### Issue processor (batch, then exit)
239: 
240: ```bash
241: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
242: ```
243: 
244: The processor (`process-issues.sh`) iterates all open issues from hardcoded repos, piping each issue number into `opencode run`. Configure which repos to scan by editing `process-issues.sh`.
245: 
246: ### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)
247: 
248: ```bash
249: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/30 \
250:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
251:   make plan
252: ```
253: 
254: The planner (`plan-issue.sh`) parses the issue URL to extract owner/repo/number, clones the repo, then pipes a prompt into `opencode run` instructing it to read the issue, understand the codebase, and post a plan as a GitHub comment.
255: 
256: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
257: 
258: ```bash
259: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
260: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
261:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
262:   -e ISSUE=42 \
263:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
264:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
265:   /script.sh
266: 
267: # Pass an inline command instead:
268: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
269:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
270:   -e ISSUE=42 \
271:   sh -c 'echo "Issue: $ISSUE" && cat README.md'
272: ```
273: 
274: The worker (`generic-worker.sh`):
275: 1. Validates `REPO_URL` is set
276: 2. Clones the repo to `WORK_DIR` (default `/repo`)
277: 3. If `/opencode-config` exists (from a mounted volume), copies it to `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` to bootstrap custom agent definitions
278: 4. Exports `ISSUE` as an environment variable
279: 5. Executes the provided command (or exits with clone info if no command given)
280: 
281: **Security**: `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` are passed from the host environment and never read into agent context.
282: 
283: ## Testing
284: 
285: ```bash
286: make build    # Build all images first (required)
287: make test     # Run shellcheck + all integration tests
288: make verify-quickstart  # Full quickstart verification (build → serve → curl → cleanup)
289: ```
290: 
291: The test suite (`tests/`) exercises:
292: 
293: | Test file | What it validates |
294: |---|---|---|
295: | `test-serve.sh` | `opencode-serve --help` returns help text; health-check endpoint returns `{"healthy":true}` |
296: | `test-web.sh` | `opencode-web --help` returns help text; health-check endpoint returns `{"healthy":true}` |
297: | `test-acp.sh` | socat binary is present, opencode binary is present, TCP listener on port 4097 is reachable |
298: | `test-generic-worker.sh` | Missing `REPO_URL` triggers error; clone-and-inspect on a public repo |
299: | `test-issue-processor.sh` | Missing `GH_TOKEN` triggers error |
300: | `test-plan-issue.sh` | Missing `ISSUE_URL` triggers error |
301: | `verify-quickstart.sh` | E2E: `make build`, `make serve`, curl health-check `{"healthy":true}`, `make stop` |
302: | `generic-worker/run-tests.sh` | Extended agent harness + repo inspection (requires `GH_TOKEN`). Runs as part of `make test` when `GH_TOKEN` is set. |
303: 
304: ### Extended generic-worker test suite
305: 
306: The `tests/generic-worker/` directory contains an extended integration test suite for the generic worker container:
307: 
308: | File | Purpose |
309: |---|---|
310: | `run-tests.sh` | Test runner: invokes both harnesses inside the container |
311: | `.harness/agent_test.sh` | Bootstraps a custom agent and runs `opencode run --agent test` |
312: | `.harness/repo_inspect.sh` | Non-destructive: git log, file count, README check on a cloned repo |
313: | `agent/test.md` | Custom test agent definition ("test" agent) |
314: | `.made/workflows.yml` | Workflow definition metadata |
315: 
316: These tests require `GH_TOKEN` for GitHub operations and are skipped by `make test` if the token is unavailable. Run them explicitly:
317: 
318: ```bash
319: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make test-generic-worker
320: ```
321: 
322: ### Workflow harness tests
323: 
324: The `workflows/issue-resolution/` directory contains a continuous issue-resolution workflow:
325: 
326: | Path | Purpose |
327: |---|---|
328: | `.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` | Full issue lifecycle: check issues, sync, fix, commit, review, merge |
329: | `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` | OpenCode config for the workflow (Context7 + sequential thinking MCP) |
330: | `.opencode/agent/review.md` | Custom review agent definition |
331: | `.opencode/commands/` | Command files: `prp-issue-fix.md`, `prp-review.md`, `commit-push.md`, `resolve-ci-errors.md`, and `ghar-*` variants |
332: | `.made/workflows.yml` | Workflow metadata |
333: 
334: Run the continuous resolution workflow inside the generic-worker:
335: 
336: ```bash
337: docker compose run --rm \
338:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
339:   -e GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
340:   -v "$(pwd)/workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro" \
341:   opencode-generic-worker \
342:   /path/to/continuous-issue-resolution.sh
343: ```
344: 
345: ## Security Rules
346: 
347: 1. **Never hardcode `GH_TOKEN`** in Dockerfiles or scripts. Always pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` from the calling shell.
348: 2. **Change the default password** in production: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` to a strong value.
349: 3. **`profiles: [manual]`** containers must be run with `docker compose run --rm` — never started by `docker compose up`.
350: 4. **Container entrypoints use `set -euo pipefail`** and validate required environment variables before proceeding.
351: 5. **Secrets never enter agent context** — runner containers pass tokens as env vars only, not as part of agent prompts.
352: 
353: ## Prerequisites
354: 
355: | Tool | Minimum version | Purpose |
356: |---|---|---|
357: | [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) | 24+ (Compose v2) | Container runtime |
358: | [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) | 2.x | GitHub authentication for runner containers |
359: 
360: Docker must be installed and the Docker socket accessible. The `gh` CLI is only required if you use the runner containers (`issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`).
361: 
362: ## Project Structure
363: 
364: ```
365: .
366: ├── serve.dockerfile          # HTTP server image
367: ├── web.dockerfile            # Web UI server image
368: ├── acp.dockerfile            # ACP protocol bridge image
369: ├── issue-processor.dockerfile # Batch issue processor image
370: ├── plan-issue.dockerfile      # Single-issue planner image
371: ├── generic-worker.dockerfile  # Generic clone-and-exec worker image
372: ├── generic-worker.sh          # Entrypoint script for generic-worker
373: ├── plan-issue.sh              # Entrypoint script for plan-issue
374: ├── process-issues.sh          # Entrypoint script for issue-processor
375: ├── docker-compose.yml         # All service definitions, volumes, profiles
376: ├── Makefile                   # All make targets (build/run/test/lint/clean/verify-quickstart)
377: ├── tests/                     # Integration test suite
378: │   ├── test-serve.sh
379: │   ├── test-web.sh
380: │   ├── test-acp.sh
381: │   ├── test-generic-worker.sh
382: │   ├── test-issue-processor.sh
383: │   ├── test-plan-issue.sh
384: │   ├── verify-quickstart.sh
385: │   └── generic-worker/        # Extended generic-worker tests
386: │       ├── run-tests.sh
387: │       ├── .harness/          # Test harness scripts
388: │       └── agent/             # Custom test agent definitions
389: ├── workflows/                 # Workflow harness definitions
390: │   └── issue-resolution/      # Continuous issue resolution workflow
391: │       ├── .harness/
392: │       ├── .opencode/         # OpenCode config, agents, commands
393: │       └── .made/
394: └── AGENTS.md                  # Project-level agent instructions
395: ```
396: 
397: ## Dockerfiles detail
398: 
399: ### Base pattern (all containers)
400: 
401: ```dockerfile
402: FROM node:22-slim
403: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
404:     git ca-certificates [socat] [curl] && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
405: RUN npm install -g opencode-ai@latest
406: ```
407: 
408: ### Serve & Web
409: 
410: ```dockerfile
411: ENV OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD=changeme
412: EXPOSE 4096
413: ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve"]
414: CMD ["--port", "4096", "--hostname", "0.0.0.0"]
415: ```
416: 
417: ### ACP
418: 
419: ```dockerfile
420: EXPOSE 4097
421: CMD socat TCP-LISTEN:4097,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"opencode acp",pty,stderr
422: ```
423: 
424: No `ENTRYPOINT` — uses `CMD` directly so socat is the main process.
425: 
426: ### Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker)
427: 
428: ```dockerfile
429: ARG TARGETARCH
430: RUN case "$TARGETARCH" in ... download gh CLI ... esac
431: COPY *.sh /usr/local/bin/
432: CMD ["/usr/local/bin/script.sh"]  # or ENTRYPOINT for generic-worker
433: ```
434:

436:

# opencode-container

Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.

## Quickstart

**Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).

```bash
make build
make serve
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
```

That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.
